errors.evidence: The vertical axis in the figure ranges from 0 to 40, not 0 to 30.
The tick marks on the vertical axis are at intervals of 5 (e.g., 0, 5, 10, 15, etc.), not 10.
The XLM-B₂ bar for Uralic is below 5, not approximately 19.
The description does not mention that the Semitic group has the largest error bars for all its bars.
The description does not mention that each group within a category is visually separated, facilitating model-wise comparison.
The description does not explicitly state that the chart illustrates the effect on different language families.

errors.text_span: For IE-Baltic, all six bars are relatively short, ranging from approximately 1 to 5. For IE-Germanic, the bars range from near 0 (mBERT-R₂) to approximately 15 (XLM-B₂), with mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ both near 10. IE-Indic shows the tallest bars overall, with mBERT-B₂ reaching approximately 24, XLM-B₂ approximately 21, mBERT-R₂ approximately 21, and XLM-R₂ approximately 18, while mBERT-L₂ is near 1 and XLM-L₂ near 5. IE-Romance bars range from near 0 to approximately 13, with the B₂ variants being tallest. IE-Slavic shows bars ranging from approximately 1 to 17, with XLM-B₂ being the tallest. IE-other has bars ranging from approximately 0 to 8. Isolate shows very small bars, all near 0. Semitic displays mBERT-L₂ at approximately 11 and XLM-L₂ near 5, with the R₂ variants slightly negative and the B₂ variants near 0, accompanied by notably large error bars. Uralic shows mostly near-zero values except for XLM-B₂ at approximately 19, also with large error bars.
